name: Nectarines
why_now: Nectarines are peaches without the fuzz, and in August they often hit their stride when peach season begins to wind down. The flavor is similar — sweet, aromatic, deeply summery — but the skin is thinner and doesn't need peeling. This is the last good stone fruit window before fall.
how_to_choose: Fragrant at the stem end — this is the most reliable test
Gives slightly when gently pressed near the top
Deep color, though variety affects this (yellow and white varieties both have peak moments)
Avoid hard nectarines — they were picked underripe and won't improve meaningfully
buy_this_much: 4–5 nectarines for the week. They don't all need to be eaten at once.
price_note: Stone fruit is still affordable in August, though supply begins to thin by late in the month. Buy them when you see good ones — the window doesn't come back.

flavor_paths.name: Nearly nothing
flavor_paths.description: Sliced and eaten as they are. A pinch of flaky salt if you want to push it.

flavor_paths.name: With yogurt
flavor_paths.description: Sliced on Greek yogurt in the morning, maybe a little honey. That's it.

flavor_paths.name: On the plate
flavor_paths.description: Alongside burrata when figs aren't enough or aren't available.

weekday_uses: Sliced on Greek yogurt in the morning
Sliced alongside the weekend cheese plate
weekend_use: Alongside the fig and burrata plate — or in place of figs if they weren't available. The combination of ripe stone fruit, good cheese, and cured meat holds up in either direction.
storage: Counter until ripe. Eat within a day or two of peak ripeness. Do not refrigerate until fully ripe, and use quickly after.
one_thing_to_learn: Nectarines and peaches are genetically almost identical — the difference is a single gene that determines whether the skin is fuzzy or smooth. Their flavor profiles and peak windows are nearly the same. If you're buying from a farmers market, ask which variety the grower would eat today. They usually know exactly which ones are ready.
market_question: Which variety is ripest right now?
